sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Mexico.
Mexico is a large and colorful country in North America.
Let's learn about it in slow and simple English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Mexico?
Mexico is in North America.
It is south of the United States
and it is north of Guatemala and Belize.
It has two oceans, the Pacific Ocean
and the Gulf of Mexico.
Mexico has beaches, mountains, forests, deserts and cities.
What is the capital city of Mexico?
The capital city is Mexico City.
It is one of the biggest cities in the world.
It has many museums, parks, markets and historic buildings.
Mexico City was built on the land of an ancient Aztec city.
Other big cities are Guadalajara, Monterey, Cancun and Puebla.
How many people live in Mexico?
About 130 million people live in Mexico.
It is the second most populated country in Latin America
after Brazil.
Many people live in big cities,
but others live in small towns or in the countryside.
What language do people speak in Mexico?
People in Mexico speak Spanish.
Spanish is the official language.
Some people also speak indigenous languages
like Nahuatl, Maya, Zapotec and many others.
There are over 60 indigenous languages in Mexico.
Many people in tourist areas also speak some English.
What is the weather like in Mexico?
The weather in Mexico is different in different places.
In the north, it can be hot and dry.
In the mountains, it is cooler.
In the south, it is hot and humid.
Mexico has a rainy season from May to October
and a dry season from November to April.
What does Mexico look like?
Mexico has many types of landscapes.
Beaches with white sand and blue water,
mountains and volcanoes,
rainforests with lots of plants and animals,
deserts with cactus and rocks,
pyramids and old ruins from ancient cultures.
One famous volcano is Popocadepetal.
One famous beach area is Cancun.
What animals live in Mexico?
Mexico has many animals such as jaguars, monkeys, iguanas,
parrots, whales, sea turtles.
There are also cows, horses, goats and chickens on farms.
Mexico is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world.
What are people eat in Mexico?
Mexican food is famous and delicious.
It is full of flavor, color and spice.
People eat tortillas, flatbread made from corn or wheat,
beans and rice, chavacados, tomatoes and onions.
Popular Mexican dishes are tacos, tortilla with meat,
vegetables and salsa, tamales,
corn dough with filling, steamed in leaves,
enchiladas, tortillas rolled with sauce and cheese,
guacamole, mashed avocado with lime and salt,
pazzole soup with meat and corn.
For dessert, people enjoy churros,
flan and sweet bread.
They drink agua fresca, coffee, hot chocolate and horchata.
What is life like in Mexico?
Life in Mexico is full of family, music and tradition.
People enjoy spending time with family and friends.
Children go to school during the week.
Many people work in shops, offices, farms or tourism.
People often go to markets, walk in the plaza
or eat street food.
In the evening, people enjoy music, dancing or watching TV.
What are some holidays and traditions in Mexico?
Dia de los Muertos, Day of the Dead.
November 1 to Tech.
People remember and celebrate family members who have died.
They make altars, bring flowers and share food.
Independence Day, September 16,
there are parades, fireworks and flags.
Christmas with Posada songs and food.
Easter with processions and family meals.
Three Kings Day on January 6 with gifts and sweet bread.
Some fun facts about Mexico.
The Mexican flag is green, white and red
with an eagle in the center.
Chocolate and corn were first used in Mexico.
Mexico has ancient pyramids like Teotihuacan and Chichen Itza.
Mariachi music is traditional Mexican music with guitars and trumpets.
Mexico has 34 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Now you know many things about Mexico.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about the cities, animals, traditions and daily life.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye or as they say in Spanish.
Adios.
